non_blocking.what: On an id collision the runtime's session rule wins over the file's project rule: `{ ...file.rules, ...sessionRules }`. Probed: a session rule r-no-evening-push plus a file that has a project rule of that id leaves scope 'session' in the adopted state. The adopted project rule is then absent from repoPart(state), and the next export of rules.json drops it with no outside record. Reversible (the outside copy and git keep the file) and unreachable today (nothing creates session rules yet). FEAT-004 should refuse an id that exists under the other scope when a rule is created, or adoptRepo should refuse the collision and name it.

A measured value is carried over to the file's signal without checking it against the file's type. If the file changes a signal's type, stateProblem(next) in adoptRepoLocked refuses the whole adoption (reason names the field) and the person can only restore. Detectors cannot run yet (R6 blocked), so no `detected` value exists today. Dropping a `detected` value that no longer fits would keep adoption possible.
